image_description: A wooden staircase with white risers and treads, featuring a decorative wrought-iron balustrade with ornate red scrollwork. A smooth wooden handrail runs along the top of the ironwork, supported by vertical metal spindles and anchored by wooden newel posts at the bottom and top landings. The background shows cream-colored walls and a hardwood floor.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The railing clearly follows the diagonal incline of the stairs from bottom-left to top-right.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Continuous handrail supported by evenly spaced balusters.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A continuous wooden rail is visible atop the vertical supports. Spacing appears regular.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Balusters are slender cylindrical or turned posts of narrow diameter, closely spaced relative to their height.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vertical elements are slender metal rods/spindles, consistent with the description of narrow diameter balusters.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Handrail is smooth rounded or molded strip running parallel to staircase incline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top rail is smooth wood, rounded profile, parallel to the stair slope.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Newel posts thicker vertical supports anchor ends and corners.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Thicker wooden posts are visible at the start (bottom left) and end (top right/landing) of the railing section.
The entire structure aligns perfectly with the step geometry.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Materials range from polished wood with ornate turnings to sleek metal with minimal design.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Combination of polished wood handrail/newels and metal (painted red/black) ornate scrollwork is present.
Visual textures confirm wood grain on rails and metallic sheen/paint on balusters.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Evenly spaced vertical posts creating rhythmic pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vertical spindles create a consistent rhythmic visual pattern along the stairs.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The red ornate metal scrollwork near the bottom steps appears to float slightly or lack clear physical connection points to the vertical spindles or the stair treads. The geometry of the swirls is somewhat nonsensical structurally.
The wood grain on the handrail is extremely uniform and lacks micro-detail, appearing slightly plastic or airbrushed rather than naturally textured.
The connection between the handrail and the top newel post is slightly ambiguous; the rail seems to merge into the post without a clear joinery detail, typical of AI generation smoothing.

To audit the connectivity of the complex red metal shapes, ensuring they are physically attached to the vertical spindles and not fused/floating.

Physical grounding of the railing system to the stair treads
